# Methods

## Adjustment for the positive predictive value of suspected cases

The outbreak time series used in the outbreak-response immunization (ORI) model comprised suspected
cases meeting study-specific clinical definitions. We therefore defined the relevant positive
predictive value (PPV) as the probability of latent true typhoid among all suspected cases in an
outbreak, $\pi_o=P(D=1\mid C=1,o)$, rather than the proportion positive among patients selected for
blood culture. Blood-culture positivity is an imperfect proxy for this estimand because blood culture
has incomplete, volume-dependent sensitivity and patients selected for culture may differ from those
not tested.

We estimated blood-culture sensitivity and outbreak-specific PPV jointly in a Bayesian latent-class
model. The culture-accuracy layer included nine historical studies (577 patients) in which blood and
bone-marrow cultures were performed in the same patients. Joint outcomes—blood positive/bone-marrow
positive, blood positive/bone-marrow negative, blood negative/bone-marrow positive, and negative by
both—were modeled with a multinomial likelihood conditional on latent disease status. Blood-culture
sensitivity in study $s$ was modeled as

$$
\operatorname{logit}(Se_{BC,s})=\alpha_0+\alpha_1\log(V_s)+\tau u_s,
\qquad u_s\sim N(0,1),
$$

where $V_s$ was cultured blood volume and $\tau$ represented residual between-study heterogeneity.
The prior for the log-volume slope was informed by the Antillón et al. meta-regression. Blood- and
bone-marrow-culture specificities were assigned priors concentrated near one, while bone-marrow
sensitivity was estimated rather than treated as a perfect reference standard. Vallenas (1985) was
excluded because the joint cells reported in the source review were inconsistent with the primary
paper's marginal yields and did not identify a defensible both-negative cell.

Community PPV evidence was assembled from 107 candidate outbreak records identified through the Koh
et al. and Appiah et al. outbreak reviews. Eight independent outbreaks supplied a clinically defined
suspected-case denominator, a blood-culture-specific tested count drawn from that denominator, and a
blood-culture-positive count from the same tested subset. The audit classified 80 records as
ineligible, retained 14 for sensitivity analyses, and held five pending source reconstruction or
retrieval. Counts were corrected to blood-specific values where supported by primary reports,
including 19/54 for Neil (2012) and 56/364 for Kabwama (2017).

Population PPV was modeled hierarchically:

$$
\operatorname{logit}(\pi_o)=\mu_\pi+\sigma_\pi z_o,
\qquad z_o\sim N(0,1).
$$

To allow preferential verification, $q_{1o}$ and $q_{0o}$ denoted the probabilities of culture among
true-typhoid and non-typhoid suspected cases. Their log-odds difference was modeled as

$$
\operatorname{logit}(q_{1o})-\operatorname{logit}(q_{0o})
=\mu_\delta+\beta_{bias}B_o+\sigma_\delta z_{\delta o},
$$

where the prespecified audit grade $B_o$ was coded 0, 1, or 2 for negligible/low, moderate, or major
verification concern. Culture-positive, culture-negative, and untested counts followed a
three-category multinomial likelihood. Because aggregate testing counts do not separately identify
population PPV and preferential selection, the selection component was interpreted as
prior-dependent and evaluated under six structural assumptions: no enrichment, skeptical, base, and
permissive priors, binary rather than ordinal grades, and no grade effect.

Models were fitted in Stan using four chains, 1,500 warm-up and 1,500 retained iterations per chain,
seed 2026, target acceptance probability 0.98, and maximum tree depth 12. We report posterior medians
and 90% credible intervals (CrIs). The main fit had no divergent transitions, maximum $\widehat R$ of
1.004, and minimum bulk and tail effective sample sizes of 1,704 and 1,631, respectively.

## Propagation into the ORI model

The complete PPV posterior, rather than posterior medians, was propagated jointly with vaccine
efficacy and campaign-timing uncertainty. ORI outbreaks matching a PPV study identifier received
draws from their local $\pi_o$ posterior. For outbreaks without a direct anchor, each iteration drew
an outbreak-specific PPV from the fitted logit-normal population distribution conditional on that
iteration's $\mu_\pi$ and $\sigma_\pi$.

The primary analysis used an additive observation model, $S_t=I_t+B_t$, where $S_t$ was observed
suspected incidence, $I_t$ was latent true-typhoid incidence, and $B_t$ was a constant non-typhoid
febrile background. For each PPV draw, $B=(1-\pi)\bar S$ was subtracted from the suspected curve,
negative values were truncated, and the resulting curve was renormalized so that
$\sum_t I_t=\pi\sum_t S_t$. The vaccine acted only on $I_t$.

At a second additive level, true typhoid was represented as $I_t=X_t+P_t$, with
background/common-source typhoid $X_t$ and propagated typhoid
$P_t=R_t^P\sum_{u\ge1}w_uI_{t-u}$. Vaccination reduced both components directly, whereas only
propagated cases generated feedback through the renewal recursion. The source fraction $\theta$
allocated baseline incidence inside that shared recursion. The former post hoc calculation
$\theta A_{\mathrm{static}}+(1-\theta)A_{\mathrm{renewal}}$ was retained only as a paired historical
comparator, using the same PPV-adjusted curve and parameter draws. We distinguished the percentage reduction in
latent true typhoid from the smaller percentage reduction observable in all-cause suspected-case
surveillance. Typhoid-attributed deaths were treated as disease-specific and were not multiplied by
PPV; non-fatal cases, years lived with disability, treatment costs, and antimicrobial-resistance case
counts were PPV-adjusted.

# Results

## Culture sensitivity and outbreak PPV

Estimated blood-culture sensitivity increased from 0.56 (90% CrI 0.46–0.66) at 2 mL to 0.65
(0.56–0.73) at 5 mL and 0.72 (0.62–0.80) at 10 mL. Estimated bone-marrow-culture sensitivity was
0.92 (0.90–0.94). These results imply that observed blood-culture positivity systematically
understates the proportion of suspected patients with true typhoid.

Community PPV was strongly heterogeneous. Study-specific posterior medians ranged from 0.10 for
Dhadwal (2008) to 0.86 for Hu (2022). The fitted median PPV for a typical outbreak was 0.31 (90% CrI
0.16–0.52), with a between-outbreak logit-scale standard deviation of 1.35 (0.85–2.03). The
audit-grade selection coefficient was positive (median 0.39, 90% CrI 0.05–0.94), but the selection
hyperparameters remained substantially prior-dependent and were not interpreted as empirical proof
of preferential culture.

![Observed blood-culture positivity, PPV among cultured suspects, and selection-adjusted PPV among all suspected cases. Points show posterior medians and horizontal bars show 90% CrIs; observed positivity is plotted without an interval.](figures/fig_main_ppv_evidence.png){#fig-main-ppv-evidence width=95%}

Figure @fig-main-ppv-evidence separates three quantities that are often conflated. Correcting only
for imperfect blood-culture sensitivity raises the estimated PPV among cultured patients, while the
selection model can lower the corresponding PPV among all suspected cases when true typhoid is
preferentially cultured. The difference was largest in outbreaks assigned major verification
concern, although intervals remained wide.

## Effect on estimated ORI impact

In the base-case two-level additive analysis, ORI averted a pooled median 1,846 true typhoid cases
(95% simulation interval 644–3,742), corresponding to a 25.6% reduction in latent true typhoid and
a 7.0% reduction observable in suspected-case surveillance. The historical $\theta$-weighted
calculation gave 25.9%; the paired additive-minus-weighted difference was −0.5 percentage points
(−2.4 to 0.7) or −37 cases (−212 to 52). The similar pooled estimates mask larger
outbreak-specific differences and do not make the two formulations mechanistically equivalent.

In a separate observation-layer sensitivity using the pure-renewal propagation workflow, selection
assumptions changed estimated true cases averted from 1,511 to 2,277, while the true-typhoid
percentage reduction remained between 29.8% and 30.7% and the apparent suspected-case reduction
ranged from 5.5% to 8.9%. These values quantify PPV-selection sensitivity conditional on that
propagation workflow; they are not uncertainty limits for the primary source-plus-propagated model.

![Two-level additive ORI model versus the historical theta-weighted calculation. Panel A compares true typhoid cases averted using paired inputs and 95% simulation intervals. Panel B contrasts reductions in latent true typhoid with reductions observable in suspected-case surveillance.](figures/fig_main_ppv_impact.png){#fig-main-ppv-impact width=100%}

Four of eight direct PPV anchors matched renewal time series. Their diagnostic-testing frames were
not always numerically or temporally identical to the corresponding incidence curves; the largest
mismatch was N'Cho (2019), whose hospital testing frame contained 583 suspected patients while the
canonical outbreak curve summed to 2,744 cases. This transport step, together with the
prior-dependence of preferential verification and the assumption of a constant non-typhoid
background, remains an important limitation of the adjusted impact estimates.

# Proposed figure placement

- **Main Figure:** Figure @fig-main-ppv-impact. It communicates the manuscript-level policy result:
  suspected-case surveillance can substantially overstate absolute vaccine-preventable burden while
  understating the relative effect observable after vaccination.
- **Main or extended-data figure:** Figure @fig-main-ppv-evidence. It makes the diagnostic argument
  visually explicit and prevents readers from interpreting blood-culture positivity as PPV.
- **Supplement:** retain the blood-volume sensitivity curve and detailed hospital/community PPV
  forest plot, which are important for validation but less direct for the main ORI narrative.
